long: The bus is moving slowly through the city this morning, so I’ll probably arrive around fifteen minutes later than planned.
I found the keys in the pocket of the jacket I wore yesterday, so you can stop looking around the house for them.
The bakery near the station is closed for repairs today, so I picked up breakfast from the small place across the road instead.
I left the documents in the blue folder beside your laptop, and the signed copy is clipped to the front so it’s easy to find.
The parcel was delivered while I was out, but they left it safely behind the side gate instead of taking it back with them.
I took the earlier train because the platform was already getting crowded, and I thought it would be easier than waiting for the next one.
The client sent the final image files this morning, so I’ve added them to the shared folder and renamed everything to match the latest layout.
I saved the last slice of cake for you and put it behind the milk in the fridge so nobody else would take it by accident.
The café was completely full when I got there, but one table opened up outside after a few minutes, so I stayed for a coffee.
I moved our catch-up to later in the afternoon because the original slot became busy, but the meeting room and agenda are still the same.
The weather cleared up just after lunch, so I decided to walk back instead of waiting for another bus in the rain.
I found the charger you were looking for in the small drawer under the desk, along with a couple of cables I thought were missing.
The delivery arrived much earlier than expected, so everything is already unpacked and waiting in the storage room near the back entrance.
I changed the light bulb in the hallway after work, and it’s surprising how much brighter the whole place feels now.
I left your umbrella by the front door so I remember to bring it with me when I see you tomorrow afternoon.
The printer jammed once when I started, but I cleared the paper and it has been running normally for the last twenty minutes.
I found an old receipt inside the book you lent me, and it looks like it’s been sitting between those pages for years.
The main road was blocked near the bridge, so I took the longer route home and somehow still got back earlier than expected.
The restaurant we talked about has a table free on Saturday evening, so I can book it now if we’re still planning to go.
The library has moved the returns box to the other side of the entrance, which explains why I walked straight past it this morning.
I left the package with reception because nobody answered the door, and they said they’ll keep it behind the desk until you get back.
The call finished sooner than expected, so I’ve got enough time to make the smaller changes before the next meeting starts.
I put the spare batteries in the top drawer beside the tape and scissors, so they should be easier to find next time.
The coffee machine is working again after yesterday’s repair, although the hot water still seems a little weaker than it used to be.
I picked up dinner on the way back because the shop was still open, so there’s no need to order anything tonight.
The park was unusually quiet this morning, and with the weather finally improving it was a much nicer walk than I expected.
I found a seat near the back of the train where it’s less crowded, so I should be able to get some work done.
The latest file is the one dated today in the shared folder, and the older version is still there only for reference.
I heard the song you recommended while I was in a shop earlier, and I recognised it almost immediately from the first few seconds.
The little shop near the corner has finally reopened after being closed for weeks, and the inside looks almost exactly the same.
I made too much dinner again, so there’s plenty left in the fridge if you want to take some with you tomorrow.
The lights came back on just as I finished finding candles, so at least we know where everything is for next time.
The queue at the post office was much shorter than usual, so I managed to get everything done before the rain started.
I left the sample on your desk beside the notes, so we can compare it with the revised version when you’re back.
The station clock is still running a few minutes fast, which explains why I thought I had missed the train this morning.
I moved the chair closer to the window because the light is better there, and it’s made the room feel a little more open.
